quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The negotiations had every reason to fail, ____ somehow both sides walked away satisfied.
quests.sentence: The negotiations had every reason to fail, ____ somehow both sides walked away satisfied.
quests.hint: Both sides walking away satisfied despite every reason to fail is the surprising twist here - a reflective, slightly formal tone.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' introduces this contrast in a reflective register, much like 'but' would. 'So' would incorrectly suggest the doomed odds caused the successful outcome.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The store doesn't carry that brand anymore, ____ does it plan to restock similar items.
quests.sentence: The store doesn't carry that brand anymore, ____ does it plan to restock similar items.
quests.hint: Watch the inverted verb order after the blank - it signals which connector continues this negative statement.
quests.explanation: 'Nor' continues the negative statement with the required inversion - 'does it plan.' 'And' would need normal word order and wouldn't match this sentence as written.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The forecast promised a clear evening, ____ the fireworks were canceled anyway due to a sudden fog.
quests.sentence: The forecast promised a clear evening, ____ the fireworks were canceled anyway due to a sudden fog.
quests.hint: The cancellation despite a clear forecast is an everyday, straightforward contrast, not a formal comparison.
quests.explanation: 'But' captures this everyday contradiction between the forecast and the cancellation. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the clear forecast the cause of the cancellation.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The choir postponed its spring concert ____ half the soloists had come down with the same flu.
quests.sentence: The choir postponed its spring concert ____ half the soloists had come down with the same flu.
quests.hint: This explains the actual reason for the postponement, not an outcome or a goal.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason - the illness among soloists. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the postponement the cause of the flu.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: Half the soloists came down with the same flu, ____ the choir had no choice but to postpone its spring concert.
quests.sentence: Half the soloists came down with the same flu, ____ the choir had no choice but to postpone its spring concert.
quests.hint: This time the cause comes first, and the outcome follows.
quests.explanation: 'So' shows the flu directly led to the postponement. 'Because' would only fit if the reason came after the outcome, which isn't the order here.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The choir director scheduled two backup rehearsal dates ____ a single round of illness wouldn't derail the whole season.
quests.sentence: The choir director scheduled two backup rehearsal dates ____ a single round of illness wouldn't derail the whole season.
quests.hint: Scheduling backup dates was a deliberate step taken with a specific goal - protecting the season from future illness.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'wouldn't' expressing the intended prevention. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a forward-looking goal.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The kids practiced their instruments ____ their mother prepared dinner in the next room.
quests.sentence: The kids practiced their instruments ____ their mother prepared dinner in the next room.
quests.hint: Both activities - practicing and cooking - are happening at the same time here, in different rooms.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows two ongoing actions happening simultaneously. 'Before' or 'after' would suggest one finished before the other began, which isn't the picture here.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The volunteers kept sorting donations ____ every last box had been checked and labeled.
quests.sentence: The volunteers kept sorting donations ____ every last box had been checked and labeled.
quests.hint: The sorting continued without stopping, right up to the moment every box was done - this is about ongoing duration.
quests.explanation: 'Until' captures this continuous sorting that stops exactly when everything is checked. 'Before' would only mark a single point, missing the sense of ongoing work.
quests.grammarRule: Time - until (continuation up to a point)

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the last guest had signed the register, the wedding planner finally allowed herself to relax.
quests.sentence: ____ the last guest had signed the register, the wedding planner finally allowed herself to relax.
quests.hint: The last guest signing in is the specific trigger for her relief, not just a general point in time.
quests.explanation: 'Once' emphasizes that the final signature directly triggered her relief. 'When' could describe simple timing but doesn't capture this completion-triggers-relief relationship as precisely.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: ____ the recipe had never failed the baker before, the cake collapsed completely this time.
quests.sentence: ____ the recipe had never failed the baker before, the cake collapsed completely this time.
quests.hint: The cake collapsing despite a flawless track record is the unexpected twist here.
quests.explanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the reliable recipe and the surprising failure. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of surprising twist.

quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting trail descriptions. 'Although' would suggest the west trail climbs sharply despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship here.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ the team had lost their star player to injury in the first quarter, they still pulled off the upset.

quests.hint: Losing the star player in the first quarter is a serious setback - this deserves the stronger of the two near-identical concession connectors.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasizes the significant obstacle the team overcame. 'Although' would also technically work, but doesn't carry quite the same weight given how early and serious the loss was.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.

quests.explanation: 'Since' introduces this established fact as the basis for the routine change. 'So' would reverse the logic, making the bridge closure a result of finding alternate routes.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The warranty will be voided ____ the device is registered within thirty days of purchase.

quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the warranty depends on registration happening within thirty days. 'If' would need 'isn't registered' added to express the same meaning.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.

quests.explanation: 'Even if' shows their plan stays the same regardless of a possible weather change. 'Unless' would incorrectly suggest bad weather could actually stop the climb.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: You're free to borrow any of the tools in the shed ____ you put them back exactly where you found them.
quests.sentence: You're free to borrow any of the tools in the shed ____ you put them back exactly where you found them.
quests.hint: Putting the tools back is presented as a clear, ongoing requirement for continued borrowing.
quests.explanation: 'As long as' fits this ongoing requirement well. 'If' would also technically work but doesn't carry quite the same firm, rule-like feel.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: My phone battery was down to two percent before the flight ____ it somehow lasted the entire way.

quests.hint: This is a relaxed, spoken-style observation - the more casual of the near-identical concession connectors fits here.
quests.explanation: 'Though' feels natural in this casual, conversational tone. 'Although' means the same thing but sounds a touch more formal for chatting about a phone battery lasting longer than expected.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The grant will be renewed for a second year ____ the organization submits a full financial report by the deadline.

quests.explanation: 'Provided that' matches this formal, official register well. 'If' and 'as long as' would also technically work but feel less suited to this precise, contract-like language.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.

quests.hint: This reads like a formal, literary account - the reason follows a comma in that reflective narrative style.
